label: b-gradient-rest
_why: THE REMAINING SEVEN RUNS OF THE B GRADIENT (user-ruled 2026-09-22, after 20260922_084038_b-gradient-4x3 aborted at 6/12: "Proceed and finish all 12 runs. These were not meant to follow our regular 2+1 rules with hard stops, go through the rest."). The parent batch ran probe-sm-b152 n=3 and probe-sm-b155 n=2 before its own stop rule fired on a runoff run and killed the session. This completes the ladder: b155's third seed, then b158 and b162 at n=3 each, pooled with the parent session for the five-point read.
_the_parent: 20260922_084038_b-gradient-4x3 — read the two together with `criteria.mjs --arm 20260922_084038_b-gradient-4x3,20260922_<this>:<setup>`. The configs are the SAME FILES, unchanged and not regenerated. B 1.50's five seeds live in 20260921_154722_slide-mild-n2 + 20260921_220915_slide-mild-n3more.
_NO_HARD_STOPS_THIS_BATCH: ⚠⚠ THE STOP WATCHER IS DELIBERATELY NOT ARMED, user-ruled. The parent batch died because `stop_watch` dropped the STOP file when run 5 ended at 1.482× vanilla's 1936 GDP (1.45× at the end state, past the register's 1.38× hard ceiling) — correct per the register, and OVER-BROAD IN SCOPE, because the register ends A CONFIG while the STOP file ends THE SESSION. On a multi-config gradient that is the wrong granularity, and this schedule's whole purpose is that a broken run is still a data point. ⇒ CONSEQUENCE, STATED IN ADVANCE: a stall or a runoff will play to 1936 and be recorded as a gradient point rather than stopping anything. Nothing guards this batch except the run timeout (420 min) and the agent's own smoke checks. ⚠ Landmine L37 also applies (the watcher's register check is dead on any multi-setup schedule) and is moot here since it is not armed at all.
_the_discard_rule_STILL_APPLIES: USER-RULED 2026-09-22 and unchanged: a run whose Britain disintegrates — British GDP at 1935 below 20% of the vanilla n=16 median, i.e. below £78M — is DISCARDED from the gradient. It has never yet bound; the lowest British endpoint over the ten seeds measured so far is £243M (0.63× vanilla).

_what_the_parent_already_measured.world_gdp_end_state_medians: B 1.50 (n=5) 1.16 · B 1.52 (n=3) 0.86 · B 1.55 (n=2) 1.22 — NOT MONOTONE, the highest median at the highest B, against the parent model's predicted 1.16 → 1.09 → 0.99.
_what_the_parent_already_measured.within_config_ranges: 0.37 (n=5) · 0.49 (n=3) · 0.46 (n=2) — each EXCEEDS the entire predicted 1.50→1.62 movement of 0.41. That is the parent's pre-registered null firing.
_what_the_parent_already_measured.british_U: Across all ten seeds of B 1.50–1.55: 1.5 / 10.0 / 4.5 / 2.2 / 9.3 · 43.2 / 2.8 / 0.4 · 1.7 / 1.0%. NINE OF TEN between 0.4% and 10.0%; the sole exception is the seed whose world GDP is 0.67, inside the WEAKENED band of the reading gate (§10.83.8). The 15% target has not been approached by any run whose world economy works.
_what_the_parent_already_measured.breaks: b152 run 3 broken by runoff (GBR capital abundance, 17 consecutive years under 5% U* at a mean hoard of 1.51 against the 1.50 threshold); b155 run 5 broken by runoff (world GDP 1.45× beyond the 1.38× ceiling).

_predictions._basis: Stated before launch as the no-ceteris-paribus rule requires, and DELIBERATELY DIFFERENT from the parent's — the parent's model has already been falsified on its own first three points, so restating it would be dishonest.
_predictions.primary: PREDICT no detectable monotone fall across the five points. Specifically: b158 and b162 medians land inside 0.80–1.25, i.e. within the envelope B 1.50–1.55 already spans, and a regression of world GDP on ln B over five points returns a slope whose sign is not stable under leave-one-out.
_predictions.the_alternative_it_could_return: ⭐ The honest rival: B 1.62 is 8% above the anchor where B 1.52 was 1.3%, so it is the first point with a step large enough to clear the noise. If the parent model's slope (−5.32) is real, b162's median lands near 0.75 and b158's near 0.88, and the five points DO trend. This is what the batch is for.
_predictions.british_U_star: PREDICT Britain stays under 15% in every seed whose world GDP exceeds 0.80. If b162 produces a seed at once above 0.80 world GDP AND above 15% GBR U*, that is the first counter-example in thirteen and the most important single result of the whole line.
_predictions.breaks: PREDICT at least one broken run among the seven — the family has broken 2 of 5 at B 1.52–1.55, both by runoff. With no watcher these now play to 1936 and are recorded.
_predictions.hard_lines: The register's band is 0.66–1.38. At the parent model's slope b162 sits at 0.75 (intact); 30% steeper puts it at 0.63 (broken by stall). Both outcomes are data here, neither stops anything.

_watch: run 1 at ~5 min: marker, version, error window BY POSITION not by a time-shaped pattern, clock, queue_mix
each endpoint: world GDP ÷ the vanilla median, GBR U* as a SHARE, GBR GDP ÷ £388M (the discard test)
⚠ NO watcher is armed — the agent's smoke check is the only guard; check the session every waiter heartbeat
at the end: the five-point regression of world GDP on ln B, jackknifed, and the GBR U* census over all seventeen seeds
post-batch: preflight -Session, VERDICT.md, the SESSION_VERDICTS row, FINDINGS
_caveats: The parent session and this one are different nights on the same machine and game version. Ratios travel between them, absolute £ do not — and every figure here is a ratio to the pinned vanilla n=16 baseline.
b155's three seeds will span two sessions (runs 4-5 in the parent, run 1 here). That is a pooling of the SAME byte-identical config, which criteria.mjs supports via a comma-separated --arm.
Nothing here tests build-to-build reproducibility; the configs are rebuilt per run as always, from unchanged files.
Launch ONLY through tools/testbed/launch_detached.ps1 CALLED DIRECTLY from the PowerShell tool (landmine L30); the STOP file must be absent at launch.
⚠ Do NOT arm stop_watch.ps1 for this batch — that is the ruling, and arming it would reproduce the abort.
_run_order: b155's missing seed first (it completes a config already half-read), then b158 ×3 and b162 ×3 back to back in ascending B — the 2026-09-13 no-alternation ruling.
